items.q: In a reading group, 18 of the 24 students finished the book. What part of the group finished, as a decimal?

mistakes.why: That is 24/18, the whole over the part. Put the part on top: 18/24.
The count 18 is not a decimal of the group. Divide the part by the whole: 18/24 = 0.75.

items.q: In a class of 25 students, 2 are left-handed. What decimal of the class is left-handed?

mistakes.why: The decimal point slipped one place: 2/25 = 0.08, which is 8%, not 80%.
That is 2/100. The whole is 25 students, so divide by 25: 2/25 = 0.08.

items.q: A survey asked 400 adults whether they had visited a museum this year; 132 said yes. What decimal of the adults said yes?

mistakes.why: That divides by 1,000. The whole is 400 adults: 132/400 = 0.33.
That is 400/132, the whole over the part. Put the part on top.

items.q: Which decimal and percent equal <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: 0.38 and 38%, the same as 38 out of 100

items.q: What is 45% of 300?
Of 60 seniors, 24 play a school sport, and 9 of those 24 play two sports. What part of the sport players play two sports?
At school A, 18 of 30 students walk to school. At school B, 25 of 50 walk. Which statement is correct?
options: More of school B walks, because 25 is larger than 18
The schools are the same, since both have some walkers
A larger part of school A walks: 0.60 against 0.50
School B, because 50 students is larger than 30 students

items.q: Of 120 people at a concert, 42 bought a T-shirt. Type an expression for the percent who bought a T-shirt (for example, a fraction times 100).

mistakes.why: That is the whole over the part. The part, 42, goes on top: 42/120 * 100.
Divide by the whole, 120, not by 100: 42/120 = 0.35, then times 100 gives 35%.

items.q: Put these values in order from smallest to largest.

Which of these are equal to <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>? Select all that apply.
A survey found that 2 of every 3 students own a bike. Rounded to one decimal place, what percent own a bike?

Evaluate <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2 + 4 + 9}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That divides just the 9 by 3: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 + 4 + 3</annotation></semantics></math>. The fraction bar groups the whole top, so add first: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{15}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
That is the top alone. Finish by dividing by 3.

items.q: Evaluate <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\frac{(2 - 5)^2 + (4 - 5)^2 + (9 - 5)^2}{3 - 1}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Give two decimal places.

mistakes.why: That is the value before the square root. Finish with <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>13</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{13}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That divides by 3 instead of <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 - 1 = 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Work out the bottom as written.

The distances <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> add to 0, but each is squared first: 9, 1 and 16.

items.q: For the values <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_1 = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_2 = 5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_3 = 10</annotation></semantics></math>, what is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum x_i</annotation></semantics></math>?
What is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6 + 4 \times 3</annotation></semantics></math>?
Type an expression for the average of 12, 15, 18 and 21: add the values, then divide by how many there are.

mistakes.why: Without brackets only the 21 is divided by 4. Put the sum in brackets: (12 + 15 + 18 + 21)/4.
There are four values, so divide by 4.

items.q: What is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-3)^2</annotation></semantics></math>?
What is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>0.25</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{0.25}</annotation></semantics></math>?
Type an expression for the square root of the whole quantity 26 divided by 2.

mistakes.why: That takes the root of 26 and then divides by 2. Put the whole fraction inside the root: sqrt(26/2).
The square root is missing: sqrt(26/2).

items.q: A formula says <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{x - 50}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> when <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>62</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 62</annotation></semantics></math>?

Put the steps for evaluating <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\frac{(2 - 5)^2 + (4 - 5)^2 + (9 - 5)^2}{3 - 1}}</annotation></semantics></math> in order.

Two students evaluate <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum (x_i - 5)</annotation></semantics></math> for the values 2, 4 and 9. What do they get, and why?
options: 0: the distances from 5 above and below cancel
8, from adding the distances without their signs
15, from adding the values and ignoring the 5

items.q: A count X can be 0, 1, 2, and so on. Which inequality says "X is at least 3"?
For a count X, which is the same as "fewer than 3"?
A count X can be 0 to 6. Which values are included in "at most 2"? Select all that apply.
Out of 10 free throws, a player makes "more than 4". For the count X of free throws made, which inequality fits?
Which inequality says "no more than 5"?
A count X can be 0, 1, 2, ... , 8. Which counts make up "at least one"?
Which inequality says "from 2 to 5, inclusive"?
Which phrase means the same as <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X \ge 3</annotation></semantics></math>?
Ten students read 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9 books. How many students read at least 5 books?
For a count, "fewer than 3" and "3 or fewer" give different answers. For a commute time measured very precisely, do "less than 20 minutes" and "20 minutes or less" give very different proportions?
options: No: almost no one has a commute of exactly 20.000 minutes
Yes: "or less" adds each commute of exactly 20 minutes
Yes: one of them leaves out half of the data
No: commute times are counts, so the phrases agree

items.q: For a count X from 0 to 10, put these events in order from the fewest included values to the most.
Type an expression for the number of ways to line up 5 different books on a shelf, and check its value.

mistakes.why: That counts only the first two places. All five places are filled: 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 5!.
Once a book is placed it cannot be used again, so the choices go down: 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.

items.q: What is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4!</annotation></semantics></math>?
A quiz has 10 questions. Type an expression for the number of ways to choose which 3 questions a student gets right.

mistakes.why: That counts ordered choices. Which 3 questions are right does not depend on order, so divide by 3! = 6: 10C3.
Choosing 3 of 10 is not 10 × 3. Use the combination 10C3.

items.q: How many different teams of 2 can be chosen from 4 people?

Why does choosing 3 of 10 questions use a combination and not <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10 \times 9 \times 8</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: The order in which the 3 questions are picked does not matter

<math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10 \times 9 \times 8</annotation></semantics></math> is too large for a calculator
Combinations are used when questions can be repeated

<math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10 \times 9 \times 8</annotation></semantics></math> counts the questions answered wrong

items.q: What are <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>8</mn></msub><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_8C_0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>8</mn></msub><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>8</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_8C_8</annotation></semantics></math>?

Type an expression with factorials for <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_6C_2</annotation></semantics></math>, the number of ways to choose 2 of 6.

mistakes.why: Divide by both <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2!</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(6 - 2)! = 4!</annotation></semantics></math>: 6!/(2! * 4!).
Use factorials in the bottom: 2! and 4!, not 2 and 4.

items.q: What is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0!</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which is equal to <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>10</mn></msub><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{10}C_3</annotation></semantics></math>?
A pizza shop offers 6 toppings. How many different pizzas with exactly 3 different toppings are possible?

A line passes through the points <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 7)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>19</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(6, 19)</annotation></semantics></math>. What is its slope?

mistakes.why: That is run over rise. Slope is rise over run: (19 − 7)/(6 − 2).
That is the rise alone. Divide by the run, 6 − 2 = 4.

items.q: For the same line through <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 7)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>19</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(6, 19)</annotation></semantics></math>, what is the y-intercept?

mistakes.why: That is y at x = 2. The intercept is y at x = 0: 7 − 3(2) = 1.
That adds the slope times 2 instead of subtracting: going from x = 2 back to x = 0 lowers y by 3 × 2.

items.q: Type the expression for the slope of the line through <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 40)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>28</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(5, 28)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is run over rise. Put the change in y on top.
Subtract in the same order on top and bottom: (28 − 40)/(5 − 1).

items.q: A bike rental costs <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 12 + 3x</annotation></semantics></math> dollars for <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> hours. What does the slope 3 tell you?
options: The rental costs 3 dollars before any time is used
The cost goes up 3 dollars for each additional hour
The bike can be rented for at most 3 hours
The total cost of the rental is 3 times the hours

items.q: For the rental cost <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 12 + 3x</annotation></semantics></math>, what does the y-intercept 12 tell you?
options: The cost goes up 12 dollars for each hour
The cost is 12 dollars per hour after the first hour
The cost is 12 dollars at 0 hours, a fixed fee

items.q: Using <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 12 + 3x</annotation></semantics></math>, what is the cost of a 5-hour rental?

A cooling drink’s temperature is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2.5</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 80 - 2.5x</annotation></semantics></math> degrees after <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> minutes. What does the slope tell you?
options: The temperature rises 2.5 degrees for each minute
The temperature falls 2.5 degrees for each minute
The drink is 80 degrees colder after each minute

items.q: Which line rises most steeply?

A line for adults gives height in centimeters from shoe length in centimeters: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>95</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2.8</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 95 + 2.8x</annotation></semantics></math>. Why does the intercept 95 have no sensible meaning here?
options: A shoe length of 0 cm is impossible for an adult
The slope is positive, so the intercept is zero
Intercepts are given in different units from y

items.q: A line has slope 4 and passes through <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 20)</annotation></semantics></math>. What is its equation?
